seoTitle: DPIA Screening: Is a Data Protection Impact Assessment Needed?
metaDescription: Tick the nine high-risk criteria and see whether a DPIA is likely required, worth considering or probably not needed. Free screening aid.
intro: Applies the nine WP29/EDPB criteria and the GDPR Art. 35(3) cases to tell you whether a DPIA is likely needed.
why:
A data protection impact assessment is required when processing is likely to result in a high risk to people. The WP29 guidelines list nine criteria; processing that meets two or more will in most cases need a DPIA. Art. 35(3) names cases where one is always required, and each national authority publishes its own list.

Tick what applies and get a screening result with the reasoning to write down. It is a screening aid only. Your DPO or lawyer decides.
howTo: Describe the processing activity in your own notes.
Tick the Art. 35(3) and national list boxes if they apply.
Read the result and record the reasoning.

faq.q: What if I score one criterion?
faq.a: Review it with your DPO. A DPIA may still be needed, and writing down why or why not is good practice.
On your supervisory authority's website. This tool does not include any national list.
If high risk remains that you cannot reduce, Art. 36 requires consulting the authority first.
